mutants.description: run_counter keeps counting past max_on_counts and wraps instead of saturating at the ceiling
mutants.reason: If pwm_sync stays high, run_counter wraps to 0 after 2^ON_TIME_W - max_on_counts clocks. It then reads below the ceiling again, so pulse_allowed comes back on and pwm_out goes high again in the middle of the same stuck-high pulse.

mutants.description: The envelope is re-armed whenever the gated pulse ends, not only when pwm_sync goes low, so a truncated pulse re-arms while pwm_sync is still high
mutants.reason: When pwm_sync stays high for more than max_on_counts+1 clocks, pulse_allowed clears and the next clock takes the low-phase branch, which clears the counter and sets pulse_allowed again. pwm_out drops for one clock and then goes high again, giving the gate driver repeated pulses within one cycle.

mutants.description: The saturated-hold branch wins over the low-phase re-arm, so a counter at the ceiling is never cleared
mutants.reason: Once one pulse reaches the ceiling, run_counter stays at max_on_counts through the low phase and pulse_allowed stays 0. pwm_out then stays low for every later pulse until max_on_counts goes up.

mutants.description: The ceiling test is equality instead of less-than, so a ceiling lowered below the running count is missed
mutants.reason: If max_on_counts drops below run_counter while pwm_sync is high (soft_start resetting to the floor, or clamping to a lowered max_on_limit), the counter climbs on to wrap-around with pulse_allowed held at 1. pwm_out then follows pwm_sync far past the new ceiling.

mutants.description: pulse_allowed is decided from the post-increment count instead of the pre-edge run_counter, which removes the documented +1 clk offset
mutants.reason: For any max_on_counts of 1 or more, a pulse longer than the ceiling is cut after max_on_counts clocks instead of max_on_counts+1, so pwm_out's enforced on-time is one clock short.

mutants.description: The envelope is re-armed only once run_counter has already been cleared, one clock into the low phase, not on its first clock
mutants.reason: On the first low clock after a pulse, pulse_allowed goes to 0 while run_counter is still nonzero. If the low phase lasts only one clock (high duty), the next pulse starts with the gate closed, and pwm_out loses that pulse's first clock.

mutants.description: run_counter is cleared on the low phase only after a pulse that was truncated, so the on-time of a pulse that ended under the ceiling carries over into the next pulse
mutants.reason: After a pwm_sync pulse shorter than max_on_counts, the next pulse starts counting from the previous width, so pwm_out is cut after max_on_counts - W + 1 clocks instead of max_on_counts + 1 (or not cut at all).

mutants.description: The saturation branch clamps run_counter to the present ceiling instead of holding it, so a ceiling lowered mid-pulse pulls the elapsed count down to it
mutants.reason: If max_on_counts drops below the running count during a high phase and then rises again within the same pulse (still at or below the true elapsed count), the mutant sees run_counter < max_on_counts and re-opens pulse_allowed, so pwm_out gives a second pulse in that cycle. The original keeps the envelope closed.

mutants.description: A zero on-time ceiling is treated as 'no limit', so pulses are passed through untruncated instead of being cut to one clock
mutants.reason: With max_on_counts = 0 and pwm_sync high for several clocks, the original pwm_out is high for one clock only (max_on_counts + 1). The mutant passes the whole pulse to pwm_out.

mutants.description: The envelope is closed only when the elapsed count equals the ceiling, so the case of a ceiling that has dropped below the elapsed count leaves pulse_allowed open
mutants.reason: When max_on_counts falls below run_counter during a pulse (soft_start reloads MIN_ON_CNT on restart, or clamps to max_on_limit), the counter correctly stops but pulse_allowed stays 1, so pwm_out keeps following pwm_sync for the rest of the pulse instead of going low one clock later.

mutants.description: The output takes 'pulse in progress' from run_counter being non-zero instead of from pwm_sync, so it follows the counter's one-clock-late view of the pulse
mutants.reason: Every untruncated pulse at pwm_out starts and ends one clock later than with pwm_sync gating. A truncated pulse comes out one clock shorter. With a ceiling of 0 the counter never leaves zero, so pwm_out never goes high.
